note: Quiet USACE campground on the west shore of Lake Shelbyville, in shaded oak-hickory woods above the Opossum Creek arm; the sites nearest the water are tent-only, and the banks are steep. --Claude
summary: recreation.gov record, rates and catalog read: USACE, 64 sites (47 RV + 17 tent-only electric), 50 A at 20, water+sewer at 13, 30-100 ft; $16 ($20/$24 classes; 2026, 2027); reservable, 2-night weekend / 3-night holiday minimums, 14 in 30; showers, flush toilets, dump, water. Count 70 -> 64. Note cleaned. Waterfront: stored lakefront -> recommend LAKEVIEW (only RV 'lakefront' site 011 is ~120-150 m from the arm through forest). Pin ~270 m north of the centroid: move recommended. FCFS conflict on rec.gov left unwritten.
flags: WATERFRONT (stored lakefront, not --AWH): DOWNGRADE to LAKEVIEW recommended (or lower). The catalog's only lakefront-tagged RV site is 011 (39.442956,-88.772543, 60 ft, 30 A): imagery puts it ~120-150 m from the Opossum Creek arm through continuous forest. Every other tagged site is tent-only (012-017, 025-029, 040-043) and cannot carry the value. RV sites 002-010 are ~150 m from the arm through forest. rec.gov says only that it 'overlooks the lake shore' and 'The banks are steep and it may be difficult to get to the water from many sites.' Not measured with 3DEP (distance alone settles it).
